title: Tests we wrote down

status_definitions.held: the stated prediction's criterion is met
status_definitions.did not hold: estimate in the opposite direction, CI excluding the null
status_definitions.null: CI includes the null value - no detectable effect
status_definitions.indicative: descriptive quality check without a pre-set threshold

timing_note: 'recorded' is the modification date of the result file (the repository has no git history); 'prediction_timing' marks criteria fixed only when this ledger was written.

tests.question: Does Culpeper repeat Dioscorides' indication for the same plant more often than chance?
tests.method: label permutation of Culpeper claim sets among 136 shared species (10,000 permutations)

tests.question: Does the transmission signal survive: permutation only among plants of similar entry length (quintiles)?
tests.method: permutation only among plants of similar entry length (quintiles)

tests.question: Does the transmission signal survive: permutation only within the same botanical family (most conservative)?
tests.method: permutation only within the same botanical family (most conservative)

tests.question: Does the transmission signal survive: same test with plants merged to genus?
tests.method: same test with plants merged to genus

tests.question: Does the transmission signal survive: only high-confidence identifications?
tests.method: only high-confidence identifications

tests.question: Does the transmission signal survive: indications merged to therapeutic categories?
tests.method: indications merged to therapeutic categories

tests.question: Are persistent (both herbals) claims more often studied at all than unclaimed indications of the same plants?
tests.method: logit of >= 1 co-mentioning paper, indication FE + log plant volume, cluster-robust by plant

tests.question: Are Dioscorides-only claims more often studied at all than unclaimed indications of the same plants?
tests.method: logit of >= 1 co-mentioning paper, indication FE + log plant volume, cluster-robust by plant

tests.question: Same, with an exact within-plant comparison?
tests.method: conditional logit, strata = plant, + log indication volume

tests.question: Are persistent claims studied more intensively (more co-mentioning papers)?
tests.method: Poisson GLM, indication FE + offset log(expected), cluster-robust

tests.question: Are persistent claims studied more intensively (more co-mentioning papers)?
tests.method: Poisson GLM, offset only (secondary)

tests.question: Are persistent claims studied more intensively once studied?
tests.method: Poisson FE restricted to pairs with >= 1 paper (intensity once studied)

tests.question: Within each plant, do claimed indications have higher lift over expectation than unclaimed ones?
tests.method: within-plant signed-rank test of mean log2 lift, claimed vs unclaimed

tests.question: Is the share of persistent (both herbals) pairs with >= 1 paper higher than for the unclaimed indications of exactly the same plants?
tests.prediction: claimed share's 95% CI above the matched share's 95% CI
tests.method: matched controls, cluster-bootstrap CIs (resampling plants)

tests.question: Intensity result with high-confidence plants only?

tests.question: Is the lead ranking robust to identification uncertainty?
tests.method: score x certainty (high 1, medium 0.6, low 0.3, genus 0.5; weakest link of the two herbals), same diversification
tests.result: tau-b 0.56 over 517 candidates; 41/60 stay in the top 60

tests.question: Are a lead plant's active targets more often associated with its historical indication than with other diseases?
tests.prediction: lead disease above the plant's median over other diseases in > 50% of leads
tests.method: LOTUS -> ChEMBL (pChEMBL >= 6, human) -> Open Targets score >= 0.1
tests.result: 33/60 leads have a path; lead disease above median in 22/51
